name: Tlaxcala (Mexico)

colors.symbolism: the castle, crowns and letters of the arms

description: A red field crossed by a broad white diagonal band rising from the lower hoist to the upper fly, bearing the state coat of arms of Tlaxcala at the centre.
history: Tlaxcala has no separately legislated state flag; the design shown — the state coat of arms on a white field — is in de facto use to represent the state.

features.role: broad white band rising from the lower hoist to the upper fly

features.symbolism: The arms combine the heraldic charges granted to Tlaxcala by Charles V in 1535 in recognition of its alliance with Hernán Cortés against the Aztec Empire (including the castle, palms and the letters of the Catholic monarchs) with indigenous Tlaxcalan symbols, marking the state's foundational role in the conquest and Christianisation of New Spain.
